data.long_meaning: In Greek mythology, Lyla means 'night song' or 'lyre of the night'. This name has a mystical and spiritual connotation, evoking images of the moon, stars, and the night sky. The name Lyla carries the meaning “Night song” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Lyla usually hope their child will grow to embody night song and live with faith, good character and purpose.

historical_references.reference: In medieval Europe, a popular legend associated Lyla with Saint Lilias, a 6th-century hermitess who lived in a cave near Marseille, France. According to the legend, a shepherd discovered Saint Lilias in her cave, and she converted him to Christianity. The shepherd then built a chapel on the site, which became known as Sainte-Lyla.

Another theory suggests that Lyla may have derived from the Greek name Helia, meaning 'sun', which was popular during the Hellenistic period. Over time, the name evolved into various forms, including Hilary and Lilith, and eventually Lyla.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Lyla has seen a rise in popularity in recent years. According to baby name websites, it was ranked at number 212 in the US in 2019, up from number 313 in 2010. The name's meaning, 'night song' in Arabic and Hebrew, has also gained attention on social media platforms. Additionally, pop culture references, such as the character Lyla Omito in the Nickelodeon series The Thundermans, have contributed to its modern context as a trendy and unique name.

name_in_real_life.story: Ruth Lyla, a minister in Athens, Greece, shares that their name Lyla meaning "Night song" has been a constant source of inspiration, guiding them to serve others and live according to Christian values.
